data.title: King Faisal University Concludes Third International Conference on Food Security and Environmental Sustainability with 10 Recommendations
data.content:
Al-Ahsa, November 20, 2026, SPA -- King Faisal University concluded on Wednesday the Third International Conference on Food Security and Environmental Sustainability, held under the patronage of Governor of Eastern Region Prince Saud bin Naif bin Abdulaziz and inaugurated by Governor of Al-Ahsa Prince Saud bin Talal bin Badr. The conference took place from November 16 to 18, 2026, with more than 500 researchers and experts from 30 countries in attendance.
    Chair of the conference's scientific committee and Dean of the College of Agricultural and Food Sciences Dr. Ahmed Saud Al-Saqufi stated that the conference concluded with 10 recommendations. Key recommendations included accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence across the food security system within national governance frameworks; establishing integrated national platforms for agricultural and climate data to support early warning systems; and expanding the application of precision agriculture and smart livestock production to enhance productivity and optimize resource use.
    Dr. Al-Saqufi said that the recommendations also called for implementing programs to reduce food loss and waste; developing sustainable food packaging alternatives through partnerships between universities and the private sector; and advancing the circular economy through waste recovery and reuse. They also emphasized reducing emissions by adopting low-carbon agricultural practices and expanding renewable energy use, as well as protecting biodiversity in marine and coastal ecosystems to support the blue economy.
    He added that the recommendations highlighted the importance of supporting multidisciplinary research and translating its findings into practical applications, alongside developing national talent in artificial intelligence, data science, and agricultural technologies.
    He noted that the conference featured more than 200 research papers, 12 scientific sessions, and 10 workshops addressing two main themes: “Artificial Intelligence in Food Security” and “Environmental Sustainability and Carbon Capture.”
    An accompanying exhibition gave participating organizations a platform to showcase their initiatives in food security and environmental sustainability. These activities opened new avenues for collaboration between universities and relevant sectors, as well as for developing joint research projects that contribute to practical solutions to food and environmental challenges.
    The third edition of the conference reflects King Faisal University's institutional identity, which places food security and environmental sustainability at the heart of its research priorities. It also underscores the university's commitment to expanding research collaboration with its partners.
    -- SPA
